name: אֲדֹנִירָם
summary: The son of Abda, the officer over the forced labour under David, Solomon and Rehoboam. Solomon set him over the thirty thousand sent in turns to Lebanon; when the ten tribes refused Rehoboam, the king sent him to them and all Israel stoned him to death. The name is אֲדֹנִי “my lord” with רָם “high, exalted”, a sentence like אֲבִירָם and יְהוֹרָם: “my lord is exalted”, as the psalms say of Yahweh. Samuel and Kings also write it short, אֲדֹרָם, and Chronicles הֲדֹרָם.

evidence.note: “אֲדֹנִירָם the son of Abda was over the forced labour.”
Ten thousand a month in Lebanon, “and אֲדֹנִירָם was over the forced labour”.
Under David, in the short form: וַאֲדֹרָם עַל־הַמַּס.
Rehoboam sent אֲדֹרָם, “who was over the forced labour, and all Israel stoned him with stones, and he died”.
The same event, the name written הֲדֹרָם.
רָם עַל־כָּל־גּוֹיִם יַהְוֶה, “Yahweh is exalted above all nations”: the second half of the name, said of the Lord.
אֲדֹנָי on a throne רָם וְנִשָּׂא, “high and lifted up”.

note: TIPNR has one person under the key Adoram@2Sa.20.24, with the forms Adoram, Adoniram and Hadoram; the entry follows it in taking the officer of the three reigns as one man, which scripture does not say outright. BDB’s a.be.ak is the short form אֲדֹרָם; its redirect a.bf.ai has no tokens and is not listed. הֲדֹרָם (2Ch 10:18) is filed under another BDB key and is not claimed here; it may be a different name (as Hadoram of Gen 10:27) given to the same man. No entry for רום exists yet to link the second element to.
